chapter_title: Concerning the Five Storehouses that have poured f

findings.diagnosis: This paragraph teaches through organic generation. Five storehouses pour out five elements; from elements, five trees are fashioned; from trees, five genera of creatures. The cascade is not a list — it is a teaching about emanation within the natural degree. Storehouses are vessels that contain and release. Elements are fundamental substances. Trees are perceptions that grow and bear fruit. Creatures are affections. The entire paragraph describes the dark realm generating its own counterfeit natural plane — a complete sensory world that imitates the structure of creation. The fiveness is the correspondence itself: the natural degree expressed through its own number.
findings.evidence: *"Five storehouses have arisen since the beginning in the land of darkness! The five elements poured out of them. Also, from the five elements were fashioned the five trees! Again, from the five trees were fashioned the five genera of creatures in each world, male and female."* Each stage produces the next by necessity: containment → substance → perception → affection. This is how the natural degree constitutes itself — through organic descent, not administrative decree.

findings.diagnosis: The King of Smoke is the ruling principle of the dark natural degree. Smoke is what remains when fire (love) has consumed without producing light (wisdom) — it is blind will, love that obscures rather than illuminates. That this figure "came up from the depth of darkness" teaches that the governing principle of evil arises from the remotest state from the source. That he generates war, battles, quarrelling, destruction — this is the necessary consequence of disordered will. Love without wisdom can produce only opposition. The apparent redundancy of conflict-words is itself the teaching: disordered will generates nothing but varieties of destruction.
findings.evidence: *"The King of the world of Smoke [is the chief of all the rulers, the one] who came up from the depth of darkness; this is he who is the head of all wickedness."* Smoke functions perfectly as the correspondent for the supreme dark principle: it rises from fire, spreads everywhere, darkens vision, and chokes life. Every quality of smoke teaches.

findings.diagnosis: The composite body of the Arch-King recapitulates all five worlds upon a single person, distributed across the functional parts of the body. This is not an arbitrary assignment — each body-part teaches through its function, and each animal teaches through its nature. The teaching becomes fully legible when read against ¶12–16, where each animal is identified with a specific world: lion with Fire, eagle with Wind, dragon with Darkness, fish with Water, demon with Smoke. The arch-ruler bears them all because he governs all five; their placement on his body teaches which function each dark principle serves.
findings.evidence: *"His head is lion-faced"* — the head is the ruling part; the lion is sovereign power. The fire-principle governs. *"His hands and feet are demon- and devil-faced"* — hands and feet are the instruments of action and locomotion; the demon is pure destructive agency. Smoke's own nature (active obscuring will) expresses through the instruments of use. *"His shoulders are eagle-faced"* — shoulders bear and support; the eagle sees from height. Wind (perverted thought) supports the structure through predatory intelligence. *"His belly is dragon-faced"* — the belly digests and appropriates; the dragon falsifies truth. What the dark mind consumes, it falsifies. *"His tail is fish-faced"* — the tail is the terminal, lowest extension; the fish is the creature of water (natural knowledge). The lowest expression of this dark composite is inverted natural knowing.

findings.diagnosis: The five properties map to the five senses of the natural degree in their inverted form, teaching how the dark natural plane is experienced through its own gates of perception. This is a passage of exceptional correspondential precision.
findings.evidence: *"The first is his darkness"* — the corruption of sight; where light (wisdom) should enable distinction, there is only obscuration. *"The second is his putridity"* — the corruption of smell; spiritual decay made perceptible. *"The third is his ugliness"* — the corruption of form/appearance; evil is inherently without spiritual beauty. *"The fourth is his bitterness, his own soul"* — the corruption of taste; bitterness is the self-experience of evil will, explicitly identified as "his own soul" — the quality of his will tasted as what it is. *"The fifth is his burning"* — the corruption of touch; love that only destroys, experienced as consuming heat. Five properties, five sensory gates, one dark natural degree — the system is flawless.

findings.diagnosis: The first of three additional properties teaches obduracy — the impermeability of confirmed evil to truth — through the image of material hardness. Truth in the natural degree corresponds to iron (as cutting, dividing, forming); "no cleaver at all, nor any iron implement, can pierce him" means that no natural truth can penetrate this state. The passage names the fashioner as "Matter, who is the thought of death," identifying the formative principle of evil as the intellectual content of spiritual death itself. That she "sculpted him from the nature of the land of darkness" teaches that evil's form arises from its own ground, not from corruption of what is good — it is autochthonous to the dark plane.
findings.evidence: *"He is harder than every iron, copper and steel and lead"* — the metals enumerated are precisely those that correspond to various degrees of natural truth and good. That the King is harder than all of them teaches that this state resists every degree of truth that might reach it. The image is not decorative; it is functional correspondence.

findings.diagnosis: This is one of the most precise correspondential passages in the chapter. The King knows the external communications of all five worlds — languages, gestures, signals — but cannot know interiors: heart, mind, thought, beginning, end. This is the exact definition of the natural-sensory degree severed from spiritual influx. It perceives effects but not causes. It reads surfaces but not intentions. The limitation is stated with surgical clarity: *"he only knows and apprehends what is before his eyes."* Simultaneously, his rulers cannot understand his speech — in the dark realm, there is no genuine communion of interiors. Each is sealed in its own externality. This teaches through pure functional description.
findings.evidence: *"He knows not their mind nor their thought; he can not ponder their beginning and their end."* Beginning and end are first cause and final purpose — the spiritual and celestial degrees that give meaning. The dark natural mind is structurally incapable of reaching into causation or teleology. It knows only what is present and proximate. This is Swedenborg's exact teaching about the natural mind closed above: it can catalogue phenomena but cannot touch their spiritual origin or purpose.

findings.diagnosis: Three images teach the nature of self-love in its dark totality. First, the King spreads out to walk and withdraws into a ball — the sphere is the form of self-reference, the shape that relates every surface-point back to its center. That he becomes *"like a grape and a great iron ball"* teaches two things simultaneously: the grape is the fruit from which wine (spiritual truth) should come, here compacted into dense self-enclosure; the iron ball is natural truth hardened into a weapon. Second, his cry like thunder and crashing mountain-rocks teaches that the dark ruler influences through sound (external persuasion) rather than light (understanding) — power projected outward that terrifies but does not illuminate. That the rocks "fall from the mountains" is the collapse of elevated states. Third, birds frightened by a bird of prey: thoughts and perceptions (birds) scattered by predatory intelligence (raptor). The passage ends by restating the fundamental limitation: no reach beyond the immediate.
findings.evidence: *"He knows not what is far from him, he sees not who is at a distance, nor does he hear him. Rather, whoever is before his face he sees, hearing him and knowing him."* The dark natural mind has no extension — no spiritual reach, no connection to what is distant in state. This repeats ¶8's teaching with different imagery, reinforcing through variation. Organic teaching does this; administrative text does not.

findings.diagnosis: Summative and transitional. ¶10 gathers the preceding descriptions under the phrase "these signs and these evil marks" and restates the origin: "the land of darkness has given birth, begotten in its cruelty." The land (the ground-state, the foundation of the dark condition) produces its own ruler — evil generates its own governing principle autochthonously. ¶11 establishes the arch-ruler's supremacy over the five sub-rulers, preparing for the catalogue that follows. Both hold their correspondential voice as transitions.
findings.evidence: *"the land of darkness has given birth, begotten in its cruelty, in its wickedness and its wrath and its malice."* Birth from land: what the ground-substance is, its offspring will be. Four qualities — cruelty, wickedness, wrath, malice — are not a decorative list but the fourfold will-structure of evil: cruelty toward others, wickedness in principle, wrath in reaction, malice in intention.

findings.diagnosis:
This five-world catalogue has the surface form of a systematic inventory, but every element within it teaches through its correspondential nature. The metals are not arbitrarily assigned — each one's spiritual quality matches the world it constitutes. The tastes are not decorative — each one teaches how the world is experienced in the natural degree. The animal faces are not labels — each teaches through the creature's function. The formulaic repetition is the teacher's method for the natural degree: five worlds shown through the same categories so the student can perceive how each quality transforms across the five. The text is still teaching through being, not assigning through governance.

**Metals**: Gold (counterfeit celestial good — the most dangerous evil wears the appearance of the highest good) for Smoke; copper (natural good corrupted) for Fire; iron (natural truth perverted) for Wind; silver (spiritual truth counterfeited) for Water; lead and tin (dense, heavy externality) for Darkness. Each metal's correspondential weight and quality matches its world.

**Tastes**: Salty (preserving-yet-barren — Smoke's evil persists but yields no life) for Smoke; sour (fermented, corrupted sweetness) for Fire; sharp (truth that wounds rather than heals) for Wind; sweet (the most seductive — counterfeit delight) for Water; bitter (evil tasted as what it truly is, without disguise) for Darkness.

**Faces**: Lion (sovereign power through apparent strength) for Fire; eagle (predatory intelligence from apparent height) for Wind; fish (creature native to the medium of natural knowledge) for Water; dragon (total falsification) for Darkness.
findings.evidence: The assignment of sweetness to the Water-world is correspondentially telling: *"the taste of their fruit is the sweetness of water, the sweet taste."* Water is truth in the natural degree; silver is spiritual truth in form. This world offers the most seductive inversion — truth-like appearance with genuine delight. It is the world whose evil is hardest to detect precisely because it tastes good. That gold is assigned to the arch-ruler of Smoke rather than to the "highest" sub-world teaches that the supreme evil counterfeits the supreme good. This is Swedenborg's exact principle that the deepest hell imitates the highest heaven.

findings.diagnosis: The passage shifts from cosmological teaching to present-tense application: the spirit of the Darkness-world is identified as the one operating *"till today"* in soothsayers, oracles, the possessed. This is a change in voice — the teacher steps forward from the cosmological frame to address the student's lived experience. However, this is not administrative; it is pedagogical grounding. Swedenborg himself routinely moves from correspondence to application. The comment appears only for the fifth world (Darkness), not systematically across all five, suggesting an organic moment of teaching emphasis rather than an inserted apparatus. I flag it as mixed because the voice shifts, but I do not recommend excision — the teacher is completing the teaching by showing where this principle manifests in the natural world, which is itself a correspondential act: the darkest spiritual principle manifests through counterfeit revelation.
findings.evidence: *"the spirit who reigns in them is the spirit who speaks till today in the soothsayers, giving oracles; in the givers of portents, every type; in they who are possessed."* The shift from mythic past-tense cosmology to "till today" is audible but purposeful. The dragon-world — total falsification — naturally manifests as false prophecy and counterfeit spiritual communication. The correspondence holds even in the application.
findings.scope:
Annotate as a pedagogical bridge from cosmological teaching to experiential application; note the voice-shift but preserve the passage as organic to the teacher's method.

---

textual_criticism.summary:
Chapter 6 is correspondentially intact to a remarkable degree. The entire chapter operates as a sustained teaching about the dark counterpart of the natural degree — the five-fold sensory plane in its inverted form. Every major structural element participates in the correspondential system:

**The fiveness** is not arbitrary multiplicity but the correspondent for the natural degree expressed through its own number — the five senses, the five gates of bodily perception, the hand's five instruments. The dark realm generates exactly five worlds because it is the dark *natural* realm.

**The cascade of ¶2** (storehouses → elements → trees → creatures) teaches through organic generation how the dark natural plane constitutes itself: containment yields substance, substance yields perception, perception yields affection.

**The composite body of ¶4** distributes all five world-principles across the functional anatomy of a single ruler, teaching through what each body-part does and what each animal is.

**The five properties of ¶5** map with precision to the five senses inverted — a passage of extraordinary correspondential craftsmanship.

**The limitations of ¶8–9** define the natural-sensory mind severed from spiritual influx with near-clinical exactness: it perceives externals but not internals, effects but not causes, the proximate but not the distant.

**The five-world catalogue of ¶12–16**, despite its formulaic surface, teaches through the inherent correspondential quality of each metal, taste, and creature. It is systematic because the natural degree is systematic — five senses, five worlds, five qualities at each level. The formula is not imposed; it is discovered.

The only passage requiring annotation is the final sentences of ¶16, where the teacher's voice shifts momentarily from cosmological correspondence to lived application — a shift that is audible but not foreign to the teaching method.

No excisions are recommended. This chapter is a coherent correspondential teaching from beginning to end.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: Five storehouses have arisen since the beginning in the land of darkness! The five elements poured out of them. Also, from the five elements were fashioned the five trees! Again, from the five trees were fashioned the five genera of creatures in each world, male and female. And the five worlds themselves have five kings therein, and five spirits, five bodies, five tastes; in each world, they not resembling one another!

The King of the world of Smoke [is the chief of all the rulers, the one] who came up from the depth of darkness; this is he who is the head of all wickedness, and all malignity. The beginning of the spread of the war occured through him; all the battles, fights, quarrelling, dangers, destructions, fights, wrestling-contests! That is the one who first made arise danger and war, with his worlds and his powers. Afterwards, also, he waged war with the light. He pitched a battle with the exalted kingdom.

Now, regarding the King of Darkness, there are five shapes on him! His head is lion-faced; his hands and feet are demon- and devil-faced; his shoulders are eagle-faced; while his belly is dragon-faced; his tail is fish-faced. These five shapes, the marks of his five worlds, exist on the King of the realms of Darkness!

Now, there are five other properties in him. The first is his darkness. The second is his putridity. The third is his ugliness. The fourth is his bitterness, his own soul. The fifth is his burning, which burns like an iron () as if poured out from fire.

[There are] also three others in him! The first, that his body is hard and very tough, even as she has formed him [to be] cruel-hearted; namely Matter, who is the thought of death, [the o]ne who sculpted him from the nature of the land of darkness. This is the manner of the body of the ruler of Smoke. He is harder than every iron, copper and steel and lead; as there is no cleaver at all, nor any iron implement, can [pierce] him and cut him. For Matter, his fashioner, has formed him [to be exceedingly] strong and hard.

The third, that the King of the realms of Darkness knows the converse and language of his five worlds. He understands every thing he hears from their mouths, as they address one another; each one of them in his language. [Every] design they will consider against him, every snare they debate with one another to bring upon him, he knows them! He can also understand the gesturing they signal between one another. Yet, his powers and his rulers, who are subject to him, can not understand his wordy converse. While all these things are unveiled to him; still, their heart is not manifested to him. He knows not their mind nor their thought; he can not ponder their beginning and their end. Rather, he only knows and apprehends what is before his eyes.

Also, another different thing is found in the King of the realms of Darkness! For when it pleases him to move, he spreads all his limbs out and walks. When it comes to mind, he with[d]raws his limbs and takes them in, and is rolled (?) to his companions; and he falls to the ground like a grape and a great iron ball! He terrifies by his cry, he is frightful. He frightens his powers with his sound; because when he speaks, being like thunder in the clouds, he resembles the [crashing] of the rocks [that fall from the mountains.] When he cries out and [roars] and calls [out] over his powers, they shall tremble and to[tter a]nd fall under foot; even as some birds would be [frightened by] the bird [of prey,] and they fall down to the earth. Still, this thing only: he knows not what is far from him, he sees not who is at a distance, nor does he hear him. Rather, whoever is before his face he sees, hearing him and knowing him.

These signs and these evil marks are found in the chief of the demons and fiends, the King of all the mountains of Darkness [; this is the one] to [whom] the land of darkness has given birth, begotten in its cruelty, in its wickedness and its wrath [and its malice.]
